The Peace of Lodi happened before the Pa.why: Common-sense case: people say each event's date or place in the sequence of its own city or reign (Lodi 1454, the Pazzi conspiracy 1478, the bonfire 1497), but nobody writes the order of the first and last as a sentence; it follows by chaining. Without transitivity the prompt's two links do not carry it.

sources.quote: The Treaty of Lodi, or Peace of Lodi, was a peace agreement which brought to an end the Wars in Lombardy between the Venetian Republic and the Duchy of Milan, signed in the city of Lodi on 9 April 1454.
The attack took place on the morning of Sunday, 26 April 1478, during High Mass at the Duomo of Florence.

The phrase itself usually refers to the bonfire of 7 February 1497, when supporters of the Dominican friar Girolamo Savonarola collected and burned thousands of objects such as cosmetics, art, and books in the public square of Florence, Italy, on the occasion of Shrove Tuesday, martedì grasso.

sources.query: Peace of Lodi AND Bonfire of the Vanities
sources.note: With max_clause_freq 500000. The two ends of the chain are not written near each other.

The Battle of Brunanburh happened before.why: Common-sense case: each battle is described on its own with its year (937, 991, 1016); the order of the first and last is not something anyone states, it is read off by chaining the two links.

sources.quote: The Battle of Brunanburh was fought in 937 between Æthelstan, King of England, and an alliance of Olaf Guthfrithson, King of Dublin; Constantine II, King of Scotland; and Owain, King of Strathclyde.
The Battle of Maldon took place on 10 or 11 August 991 AD near Maldon beside the River Blackwater in Essex, England, during the reign of Æthelred the Unready.
The Battle of Assandun (or Ashingdon) was fought between Danish and English armies on 18 October 1016.

notes: RBox contraction paired with history-replace-0009: removes the original property, that 'happened before' is transitive. Every query becomes 'I don't know', including the three propositional ones (strong Kleene). The instance prompts say 'Given only these facts' and give both links (Lodi, Pazzi, Bonfire of the Vanities; Brunanburh, Maldon, Assandun), chosen so the conclusion is a deduction by chaining and not a sentence people write. All original answers are yes; a no-answer instance would not change under removal. Near and far unrelated queries are the revision's (contraction is exempt from Rule 7 for the near query).
